species.name: Attachment-forwarding cover-note boilerplate
species.instruction: Score whether the comment begins with a short, stand-alone forwarding/transmittal line (e.g. 'See Attached', 'See attached file(s)', 'Please see attached comments of X') that is textually separate from, and precedes, the substantive letter that follows, rather than opening directly with substantive content. 10 = the comment opens with such a transmittal preamble before the real letter body begins. 0 = the comment has no transmittal preamble at all; substantive content starts in the first sentence.
species.rationale: The transmittal-preamble pattern is strongly associated with LOW dense scores despite high scorecard scores in this slice: ROW R18 (Louisiana Chemical Association, dense_pct=.274/card_pct=.782), ROW R50 (Food & Water Watch, dense_pct=.105/card_pct=.638), ROW R34 (Southern Shrimp Alliance, dense_pct=.166/card_pct=.618) and ROW R19 (Unlearn.AI, dense_pct=.122/card_pct=.563) all open with a 'See attached'-style line. This looks like a mechanical artifact of how a letter got filed, not a marker of the letter's substance.
species.upstream_parent: submission workflow: a staffer or paralegal at an organization pastes a finished PDF letter into a regulations.gov web form via a routine copy-paste habit, rather than composing text directly in the form

species.name: Formal itemized technical/regulatory rebuttal structure
species.instruction: Score the degree to which the comment is organized as a formal point-by-point regulatory rebuttal: addressed to a named official/office, broken into discrete numbered or lettered items, each citing a specific rule paragraph, CFR subsection, AD/docket number, or service-bulletin reference, with little connective persuasive narrative between points. 10 = the entire comment is such a structured technical-correction list (e.g. 'Comment No1... Page/Paragraph/Section... What is the FAA's proposed requirement...'). 0 = the comment is continuous persuasive prose with no addressee-directed itemized rule-section corrections.
species.rationale: Corporate airworthiness-directive-style itemized technical corrections score LOW dense in this slice: ROW R25 (International Aero Engines, dense_pct=.127), ROW R36 (Embraer, dense_pct=.336), ROW R40 (Meggitt vane-thickness comment, dense_pct=.293). Compliance staff are often the most technically expert commenters, so the format could co-occur with real expertise, yet dense appears to discount it regardless.
species.upstream_parent: the submitter is a regulated entity's engineering/compliance staff responding to a routine Airworthiness Directive or product-specific technical requirement as an established business process, not an independent stakeholder building a persuasive case

species.name: Single-ask brevity with minimal elaboration
species.instruction: Score how much of the comment consists of a short, single-purpose plea or statement of position (support/oppose) with little independent factual elaboration, data, or argumentative development beyond restating the ask and a one-line reason. 10 = the comment is essentially one short paragraph whose content is almost entirely 'I support/oppose this because [one general reason], please do X.' 0 = the comment develops multiple distinct facts, data points, or argumentative steps beyond the bare ask.
species.rationale: ROW R01 (sea-turtle moratorium plea, dense_pct=.429/card_pct=.976), ROW R11 (PA motorcycle-training complaint, dense_pct=.398/card_pct=.902) and ROW R17 (HHS abortion-coverage plea, dense_pct=.517/card_pct=.972) are all short, largely single-note pleas that score very high on the scorecard while dense scores them only mid-range, well below several longer or more elaborated comments in the slice.
species.upstream_parent: submitter engaged with the docket via a quick, low-effort action (e.g. a brief comment typed directly into a simple web form) reflecting low time investment rather than sustained analysis

species.name: Scanned/OCR text legibility (signal vs. noise)
species.instruction: Score the proportion of the comment's visible text that reads as coherent, grammatical, on-topic English prose, as opposed to garbled OCR fragments, single-word line breaks, stray characters, or illegible scanned-handwriting artifacts. 10 = the text is entirely clean, coherent prose throughout. 0 = the large majority of the visible text is unreadable noise or fragments with little or no recoverable meaning.
species.rationale: ROW R49 (handwritten scanned letter, almost entirely illegible OCR noise, dense_pct=.105, the lowest dense score in the whole slice) and ROW R50 (letter mangled into single-word-per-line fragments in its middle section, dense_pct=.105) sit at the very bottom of the dense distribution, while ROW R54 (a letter with visible OCR/margin-text noise bleeding into the paragraph flow but whose core argument remains fully legible) scores dense_pct=.880, near the top of the whole slice -- suggesting dense tracks legibility/extractability rather than a property of the argument itself.
species.upstream_parent: submission channel: physical, scanned, faxed, or handwritten mail versus born-digital electronic submission, and/or the docket back-end's PDF-to-text extraction quality

species.name: First-person credential or stake self-disclosure
species.instruction: Score how explicitly and prominently the comment establishes the writer's personal identity, credentials, professional role, or stake in the issue (e.g. 'I am a Professor...', 'I have X years of experience...', 'I represent...', naming a degree, certification, or affiliation) as a rhetorical move, independent of whether that identity is actually load-bearing for the argument's substance. 10 = the comment opens with or centers on an extended personal/professional credential or identity statement. 0 = the comment contains no self-identifying credential or stake language at all.
species.rationale: ROW R26 (a zoology professor's extensive credential paragraph, dense_pct=.901, near the very top of the slice) and ROW R33 (a Harbor School student/scuba-diver personal-identity narrative, dense_pct=.901) both pair heavy self-identification with very high dense scores; ROW R41 ('I have fished recreationally... and have a degree in Marine Biology', dense_pct=.662) shows the same pattern at a smaller scale.
species.upstream_parent: submitter's professional standing, expertise, or personal stake in the issue, and an instinct to lead with ethos-establishing credentials

species.name: Authority name-dropping / citation density
species.instruction: Score the density and prominence of named external authorities invoked in the comment -- cited reports, agencies, studies, statutes, or organizations named -- regardless of whether their substance is actually engaged, analyzed, or applied to a specific argument. 10 = the comment names or lists numerous external authorities/reports/institutions, even as a bare index or bibliography with no analysis attached. 0 = the comment makes no reference to any named external authority, study, or institution.
species.rationale: ROW R23 (a joint NHTSA CAFE comment that is literally an index of dozens of report titles -- CDC, EPA, National Academies, JD Power, National Geographic -- with almost no connecting analytical prose) still scores dense_pct=.626, well above its card_pct=.185; ROW R33 (which quotes the FAO and National Geographic by name) scores dense_pct=.901. Both show elevated dense tied to sheer citation volume rather than demonstrated synthesis.
species.upstream_parent: organizational resources: access to research staff, outside counsel, or a coalition's shared attachment library able to marshal many external citations regardless of whether they are substantively integrated into the argument

species.name: Meta-procedural commentary about the rulemaking process
species.instruction: Score how much of the comment is about the rulemaking PROCESS itself -- e.g. requesting an extension of the comment period, objecting to use of guidance documents instead of notice-and-comment rulemaking, or discussing procedural timing/authority -- rather than substantively engaging with the content of the proposed rule. 10 = the comment is primarily or entirely about process/procedure. 0 = the comment is entirely about the substance of the rule, with no procedural commentary.
species.rationale: ROW R51 (AASHTO's pure comment-period-extension request, with no engagement with the underlying NEPA rule's substance at all) scores dense_pct=.785, one of the higher dense scores in the slice despite card_pct=.334; ROW R48 (Kentucky Division for Air Quality, which argues at length that EPA should codify policy through notice-and-comment rulemaking rather than guidance memos) scores dense_pct=.539 while card_pct=.067 is the lowest card score in the entire slice.
species.upstream_parent: submitter is a repeat, institutionally sophisticated player (state agency, national association) with an ongoing relationship to and expertise in the rulemaking process itself, distinct from subject-matter expertise
all_names: Meta-procedural commentary about the rulemaking process

species.name: NGO action-alert templated phrasing
species.instruction: Score the presence of stock activist/action-alert phrasing typical of NGO mass-comment campaign tools: formulaic gratitude closings ('THANK YOU for your commitment to...'), superlative-modified statements of position ('I HIGHLY support...', 'I strongly urge...'), and emphatic capitalized keywords, especially combined with a short, largely interchangeable one-fact-plus-a-plea structure. 10 = the comment strongly exhibits this templated activist register. 0 = the comment shows no such stock phrasing.
species.rationale: ROW R01 ('PLEASE continue the current moratorium... IF extending this moratorium saves the life of even one more precious turtle', dense_pct=.429/card_pct=.976) and ROW R17 ('I applaud HHS for proposing this regulation... I urge HHS to ensure clear and conspicuous notice...', dense_pct=.517/card_pct=.972) both show this register and score extremely high on card but only mid-range on dense. ROW R13 shows the same closing/superlative register but paired with added factual elaboration (dense_pct=.687), suggesting the template marker itself, not the underlying content, is what the scorecard is rewarding independent of dense's judgment.
species.upstream_parent: comment was generated or guided by an NGO/advocacy-group mass-comment campaign tool (e.g. a pre-filled web action alert) that supplies stock phrasing for the submitter to personalize

species.name: Embedded formal citation within personal-voice prose
species.instruction: Score whether the comment juxtaposes an otherwise personal, informal, first-person narrative voice with one or more embedded formal legal or scholarly citations (e.g. a full case citation, a parenthetical citation to a named organization, a footnoted source) that read as though inserted by someone other than the narrating voice. 10 = a clear formal citation is embedded within personal/informal prose, creating a register shift. 0 = no such embedded citation is present, or the whole comment is uniformly formal or uniformly informal with no citations at all.
species.rationale: ROW R08 (a first-person FEMA fire-claim comment styled as a personal grievance, containing a full case citation 'Castillo v. City of Las Vegas, 195 P.3d 870, 875 (N.M. Ct. App. 2008)' embedded mid-argument, dense_pct=.631) and ROW R43 (a personal-register comment about the Hawaiian Hawk that embeds parenthetical citations '(American Bird Conservancy)', '(Honolulu Zoo Society)' like footnotes in a school paper, dense_pct=.880) both show this register-shift citation pattern paired with high dense scores; the Castillo citation is also substantively on-point for R08's argument, so the upstream factor plausibly improves genuine merit too.
species.upstream_parent: the comment received legal or research assistance (e.g. an attorney or claims law firm representing a claimant, or a teacher/librarian helping a student) that supplied one or more specific supporting citations without otherwise rewriting the submitter's voice
all_names: Embedded formal citation within personal-voice prose

species.name: Direct interrogative questions addressed to the agency
species.instruction: Score the density and prominence of direct questions posed TO the agency/regulator (e.g. 'What is...?', 'Is this sufficient...?', 'Why do we have to...?') as the comment's primary rhetorical mode, as opposed to declarative statements of position or argument. 10 = the comment is structured mainly as a sequence of direct questions to the regulator. 0 = the comment contains no direct questions to the agency at all.
species.rationale: ROW R06 ('Are these all Ameri-King units...? What is the failure rate of the AK-450...?', dense_pct=.407), ROW R22 ('What is the practical legal definition and application of an affirmation...?', dense_pct=.275), and ROW R34 ('Is this sufficient for NOAA to monitor...? Would CBP...?', dense_pct=.166) all rely heavily on this interrogative technique and cluster at the low end of dense despite scoring moderately-to-highly on card (.875, .758, .618 respectively).
species.upstream_parent: comment was drafted (often by counsel or policy staff) partly to build an administrative record for potential future litigation -- posing pointed questions on the record rather than persuading -- a technique associated with regulated-industry or advocacy-org legal strategy
all_names: Direct interrogative questions addressed to the agency

species.name: Named agency official addressed with internal office routing detail
species.instruction: Score how precisely the comment targets a specific human inside the agency, judging ONLY the addressing apparatus and never the argument. 10 = the salutation names an individual official AND pins their exact internal unit or mail routing (office code, division, branch, room, mailstop), and/or the letter carries an internal cc distribution list of named staff; first-name familiarity in the salutation ('Dear Brian;') sits at the very top of the range. 5 = a named official with only a generic title and public mailing address. 0 = 'To Whom It May Concern', 'Dear Sir or Madam', 'Docket Clerk', or no addressee at all. Ignore how long or how technical the comment is.
species.rationale: R32 addresses 'Mr. Brian Kierstead, Aerospace Engineer, Engine Certification Office, ANE-142' and then slips into 'Dear Brian;'. R02 writes to the named Deputy Administrator and recounts a meeting with his Office of Vehicle Safety Compliance staff. R10 names a Senior Economist and her exact division; R20 carries a nine-name internal cc list. Against these, R35 opens 'To Wom It May Concern' and R04 'Dear Sir or Madam'. Knowing the right person's name is a fact about access and prior contact, not about whether the reasoning inside is sound - but it is exactly the kind of surface a dense reader picks up as 'this writer is inside the process'. Marked mixed because an office with the relationship often also has the expertise.
species.upstream_parent: An existing working relationship between the submitter and the specific agency office - the submitter already knows, by name, who owns this docket.
all_names: Named agency official addressed with internal office routing detail

species.name: Agency-relationship cues
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment mentions prior meetings, ongoing collaboration, earlier submissions, established partnerships, or direct exchanges with agency personnel; score 0 when it has only a generic salutation and no relationship history.
species.rationale: Relationship language can make a submission seem institutionally consequential without adding evidence about the proposal. R23 emphasizes a longstanding AASHTO-DOT partnership, R26 cites earlier submissions, and R60 reports a meeting with NHTSA staff.
species.upstream_parent: Existing relationships and insider access within the agency or docket lifecycle
all_names: Continuity references to prior filings, meetings, or pending petitions

species.name: Coordination fingerprints: naming other commenters and incorporating their filings
species.instruction: Score how much the text reveals that the writer has read the rest of the docket and is acting in concert with others. 10 = the comment names other submitters and answers them directly, adopts or incorporates another organization's comments by reference, is labeled a joint or 'et al.' submission, or is one numbered piece of a multi-part batch with a master index of exhibits. 5 = it points readers to allied organizations without engaging them. 0 = the comment shows no awareness that anyone else is commenting. Judge coordination evidence only, not the quality of the coordinated position.
species.rationale: R55 'hereby adopts and incorporates by reference' the comments of LMOGA, the American Chemistry Council and LDEQ. R30 opens 'These comments primarily respond to comments submitted by GE Avionics'. R31 refers the Service to separate letters from three named partner organizations. R51 is literally '[Batch 11 of 18]' of 'joint comments submitted by Natural Resources Defense Council et al.' with a master index of attachments. Being inside a campaign changes how a filing looks and how it lands, independently of the argument it makes. Mixed: coalitions really do marshal evidence a lone writer could not.
species.upstream_parent: Membership in a coordinated advocacy campaign or industry coalition operating a shared docket strategy with division of labour.
all_names: Coordination fingerprints: naming other commenters and incorporating their filings

species.name: Constituency-scale claims used as standing
species.instruction: Score how prominently and how quantitatively the writer states whom they speak for and how big that constituency is. 10 = an early passage puts hard numbers on the represented base - member counts, employee or job totals, market or capacity share, facility counts, revenue share, number of signatories. 5 = a qualitative representational claim with no figures ('the national voice for the industry'). 0 = no representational claim at all; the writer speaks only for themselves and offers no scale figures. Do not credit numbers used as evidence about the rule; only numbers used to establish who the writer is.
species.rationale: R10 leads with 'nearly 440 chemical distributors', '85% of the chemical distribution capacity', '155,000 direct and indirect jobs'. R33 opens with 'approximately 20,000 miners in the United States and an equivalent number in Canada'. R09 begins 'I represent 35,000 retired teachers'. R31 is 'comprised of 120 career academics, conservationists, and biologists'. Headcount is a fact about the submitter's organisational weight, not about the comment; it is a pure standing signal that a text-reading model can nonetheless see. Mixed because well-resourced bodies also write better-evidenced comments.
species.upstream_parent: Organizational resources and a dues-paying membership base, deployed as a substitute for argument-level standing.

species.name: Counsel-drafted citation and definition conventions
species.instruction: Score the density of courtroom drafting habits in the prose. 10 = statutory pincites with reporter parentheticals, 'et seq.', '(West)', Federal Register citations in full form including '(to be codified at ...)', case citations with page pincites, numbered footnotes carrying authority, defined terms introduced in quotation marks with parentheticals such as ('the IFR') or ('the Code'), and conformed '/s/' signatures. 5 = occasional formal citations without the defined-term and footnote machinery. 0 = no citations, no defined terms, no footnotes, plain lay prose. Score the drafting conventions, not whether the cited authority actually supports anything.
species.rationale: R08 (law students) writes '16 U.S.C.A. Sec. 1801 et seq. (West)' and '83 Fed. Reg. 2412 (proposed Jan. 17, 2018) (to be codified at 50 C.F.R. pt. 300)'. R28 defines 'the Code' and 'the Proposed Regulations', footnotes its own self-description and closes with two '/s/' blocks. R24 pincites Sec. 6050X(a)(2)(B) precisely. R15, a lay fire claimant, nonetheless pincites 'Castillo v. City of Las Vegas, 195 P.3d 870, 875 (N.M. Ct. App. 2008)'. Whether a lawyer held the pen is upstream of the text and orthogonal to whether the point is right. Mixed: counsel also catch real legal defects.
species.upstream_parent: Drafting by a lawyer - outside counsel, an in-house general counsel's office, or a law-school clinic - rather than by the party in interest.

species.name: Internal comment-form scaffolding keyed to rule numbering
species.instruction: Score how much the comment reads as an institutional review artifact rather than composed prose. 10 = repeated fixed-heading blocks such as 'Comment No. 1 / Page-Paragraph-Section / Comment Type: Non-Concur / What is the proposed requirement? / Rationale', an enclosure explicitly supplied 'in tabular format', or an exhaustive march down the rule's own subpart and section numbers with one item per paragraph. 5 = numbered headings that track the rule loosely. 0 = free-form prose with no scaffolding and no section-keyed enumeration. Score the scaffolding only; a scaffolded comment may be shallow and an unscaffolded one deep.
species.rationale: R23 files a document headed 'DISPOSITION OF PUBLIC COMMENTS' with 'Comment No.1 / Comment Type: Non-Concur / What is the FAA's proposed requirement or text? / Rationale'. R12 states 'Specific comments on the collection activity are included in the table below' and then runs numbered General and Specific blocks. R20 submits 'comments in the enclosure in tabular format' behind a bulleted support/oppose summary. R15 walks 'Subpart A Section 296.4 ... Subpart C 296.21(c)(2) ... Subpart D Section 296.31' one line at a time. The shape is a fingerprint of the submitter's internal process, not of insight. Mixed: an SME review pass does raise real accuracy.
species.upstream_parent: An internal multi-reviewer clearance workflow in which several subject-matter experts fill a standard comment-collection template that is then filed largely verbatim.
all_names: Internal comment-form scaffolding keyed to rule numbering

species.name: Alphanumeric part, model, and service-bulletin identifier density
species.instruction: Score how far the comment's substance rests on proprietary alphanumeric designators that only the manufacturer and the agency can resolve. 10 = the argument is unreadable without the manufacturer's own documents, e.g. engine or model codes ('V2527E-A5', 'RB211-524B4-02'), service bulletins with revision levels ('SB 25-1111432 Rev.002', '737-71-1937 RB'), and figure or paragraph pointers inside those bulletins. 5 = a few regulation-level identifiers only (a CFR part, an FMVSS number). 0 = no part, model, or bulletin identifiers anywhere. Score identifier density, not correctness.
species.rationale: R29 argues entirely from Figures 3 and 4 of 'Meggitt SB 25-1111432 Rev.002' and attaches the bulletin. R32 asks that 'V2525-D5, V2528-D5 and V2531-E5' be struck from applicability, citing NMSB V2500-ENG-72-0671. R18 turns on 'Boeing Special Attention Requirements Bulletin 737-71-1937 RB' versus '737-78-1106 RB'; R46 on 'RB211-524B4-02'. This is a marker of who the submitter is and what genre of docket they are in - the comment could be a decisive engineering correction or a trivial applicability nit and look identical. Mixed: engineering departments hold facts nobody else has.
species.upstream_parent: The submitter is a regulated manufacturer or operator with an engineering-compliance department, filing into an airworthiness-directive-style docket that functions as bilateral engineering negotiation rather than public policy debate.
all_names: Alphanumeric part, model, and service-bulletin identifier density

species.name: Named-organism decline-and-extinction register
species.instruction: Score how far the comment is written in the conservation register centred on named living creatures. 10 = one or more species are named (common or scientific) and the text runs on decline, extinction risk, habitat, nesting or breeding, bleaching, parasitism, biodiversity, and ecosystem loss. 5 = environmental subject matter with no named organism. 0 = no organism named and no conservation vocabulary at all. Score register and topic only; a comment in this register may contain no new information and one outside it may contain a great deal.
species.rationale: R14 (twelve threatened corals), R19 (Kirtland's Warbler and cowbird parasitism), R34 (Hawaiian Hawk, native forest, ROD dieback), R05 (Sacramento Mountains checkerspot butterfly) and R40 (sihek / Guam kingfisher) all sit squarely in this register, and several of them - R05 and R34 in particular - are essentially unsourced general natural history that adds no fact the agency lacks. Topic composition of the mining pool is not merit, so a channel that fires on species vocabulary is predictive-without-quality by construction.
species.upstream_parent: Docket genre - species-listing and critical-habitat rulemakings recruit a distinctive writer population and are processed through a distinctive agency workflow, independent of any individual comment's content.

species.name: Paper or image submission provenance visible as OCR debris
species.instruction: Score how visibly the text is a machine transcription of a scanned page rather than digital-native text. 10 = pervasive transcription damage - '(cid:9)' tokens, one-word-per-line spacing with stray soft hyphens, mangled letters inside real words ('Califomia', 'V/ater', 'LACIDHS', 'Alter!' for 'Alteri'), letterhead and marginalia fragments spliced mid-sentence, page furniture, postmark or envelope text interleaved with prose. 5 = occasional artifacts (a few '(cid:9)' or a broken header). 0 = clean text with no transcription damage. Score the damage only; never penalise or reward the argument that survives it.
species.rationale: R01 is a postmarked handwritten envelope transcribed into near-nonsense ('EPA DOCKET CENTER (cid:9)', 'NOV 2 1 2019'). R04 renders every single word on its own line with soft hyphens. R41 shows 'Califomia' and 'V/ater' throughout. R25 splices letterhead fragments into mid-sentence text ('MalF.Yex 4c, @D- 0.'). R60 carries '(cid:9)' and 'Sean Alter!'. Nothing about scanner quality or the postal route is evidence of merit, yet it saturates the text a reader actually sees.
species.upstream_parent: The submission channel itself - paper mailed to the docket centre, or a scanned image PDF, rather than a digital-native filing - which is a proxy for era, for postal versus electronic routing, and for the submitter's document-production infrastructure.
all_names: Paper or image submission provenance visible as OCR debris

species.name: Evidence no editor or intermediary touched the text
species.instruction: Score how plainly the text is unmediated first-person writing that no professional editor or communications staffer passed over. Evidence for a high score: uncorrected typos and misspellings, caps-lock emphasis, exclamation marks, sarcasm or rhetorical questions aimed at the agency, run-on asides, and personal rather than institutional identifiers offered as credentials (years in a trade, a named vessel or aircraft or farm, a home town, a signature with no organisational title). 10 = several of these, unmistakably. 0 = uniformly copy-edited third-person institutional prose with a titled signature block and no typographic slips. Score the mediation evidence, not whether the writer is right.
species.rationale: R19 writes 'insuffucient' and 'Unitrd States'; R38 is openly sarcastic ('How dare such people so arrogantly expect their homes ... to simply be made whole again, eh?'); R57 asks 'who is the USDA representing - Turkey??' and signs 'Fourth Generation Family Farmer'; R52 shouts 'It makes NO SENSE' and offers thirty years of charter fishing as its credential; R35 opens 'To Wom It May Concern' from a Nantucket address; R27 is ungrammatical end to end. Whether a comment passed an editor's desk is upstream of the words and says nothing about whether the point is correct. Marked mixed honestly: an editing pass does make an argument clearer, and unmediated writers do supply first-hand facts.
species.upstream_parent: Absence of a professional editor, communications shop, or any intermediary between the writer and the docket - the writer is a directly affected individual filing on their own behalf.
all_names: Evidence no editor or intermediary touched the text

species.name: Organizational scale claims
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment prominently gives concrete membership, geographic, facility, staffing, revenue, or population-reach figures; score 0 when it contains no organizational-scale self-description.
species.rationale: Quantified institutional scale appears in R07, R20, R22, and R36, potentially cueing dense attention independently of the comment’s actual reasoning.
species.upstream_parent: organizational resources and perceived representativeness

species.name: Credential and status parade
species.instruction: Score 10 when the opening prominently lists multiple degrees, certifications, fellowships, offices, titles, or years of experience; score 0 when no status or expertise signals appear.
species.rationale: Status signaling can attract model attention independently of the argument's merit. R05 lists extensive aviation credentials, while R14 foregrounds professorship, fellowship, and international expertise.
species.upstream_parent: Submitter's professional seniority, standing, and access to policymakers

species.name: Coalition coordination footprint
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies a joint campaign, many member organizations, numerous signatories, or a named coalition; score 0 when it is plainly submitted by one unaffiliated individual.
species.rationale: R08 is part of joint comments with an attachment master index, R20 lists many stakeholder entities, and R28 describes a 120-person expert working group.
species.upstream_parent: coordinated advocacy campaign and coalition resources

species.name: Professional document apparatus
species.instruction: Score 10 when the submission contains elaborate exhibits, master indexes, slide decks, service-bulletin reproductions, revision histories, or attachment-heavy packaging; score 0 for a plain standalone comment with no document-production signals.
species.rationale: Packaging can signal seriousness and raise salience even when the underlying claim is weak or routine. R39 supplies a large indexed attachment library, while R60 appends a polished eleven-slide technical presentation.
species.upstream_parent: Availability of lawyers, engineers, consultants, and professional document-production resources

species.name: Lifecycle engagement markers
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment references earlier drafts, prior comments, extensions, supplemental material, meetings, responses to other commenters, or delayed transmission; score 0 when it gives no sign of broader docket engagement.
species.rationale: R17 requests extra time after internal coordination, R19 responds to GE Avionics, R21 supplements an earlier petition after an agency inquiry, and R47 apologizes for late delivery.
species.upstream_parent: comment timing, repeated participation, and docket-lifecycle position

species.name: Operational technical granularity
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment supplies numerous model numbers, paragraph-level edits, measurements, test results, compliance sequences, or implementation constraints; score 0 when it offers only broad conclusions without operational detail.
species.rationale: R14, R21, R40, R46, and R51 provide unusually detailed equipment identifiers, measurements, testing, maintenance pathways, and implementation timelines.
species.upstream_parent: access to technical staff, proprietary records, and engineering resources

species.name: Embedded constituency experience
species.instruction: Score 10 when the author explicitly states long tenure, personal operation, affected employment, direct exposure, or responsibility for a named constituency and connects it to the topic; score 0 when no lived or sector connection is claimed.
species.rationale: R01 cites continuous vessel monitoring, R25 describes training and flight experience, R39 cites 30 years of fishing, and R44 identifies the author as a fourth-generation farmer.
species.upstream_parent: sector embeddedness and constituency standing

species.name: Universal-benefit framing
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment relies heavily on broad appeals to public good, future generations, ecosystem health, saving species, or general moral necessity without discussing specific mechanisms or tradeoffs; score 0 when it avoids generalized value language and stays narrowly provision-specific.
species.rationale: R12, R16, R27, R33, and R58 repeatedly use sweeping protection and public-benefit claims while providing little rule-specific analysis, a rhetorical pattern that may attract dense scoring without demonstrating merit.
species.upstream_parent: surface-only

species.name: Record-building cross-references
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment constructs a formal record through dense statutory or regulatory references, quoted provisions, footnotes, incorporated comments, docket citations, or linked authorities; score 0 when it contains no such formal cross-reference structure.
species.rationale: R23 uses statutory authorities and incorporated testimony, R37 incorporates multiple organizations’ comments, R53 builds arguments around statutory text, and R59 cites specific tax provisions and reporting thresholds.
species.upstream_parent: professional legal advocacy and access to counsel

species.name: First-person lived experience
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment foregrounds the writer's personal work, use, loss, observations, or stake; score 0 when it is entirely impersonal and institutional or technical.
species.rationale: Personal exposure can make prose vivid and memorable without validating its policy claims. Examples include the autobiographical accounts in R05 and R19, and the victim narrative in R42.
species.upstream_parent: Submitter's direct exposure to the regulated activity and grassroots testimonial mobilization

species.name: Coalition scale signaling
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment emphasizes membership counts, geographic reach, signatories, or numerous represented organizations; score 0 when it comes from an unrepresented individual with no constituency claims.
species.rationale: Large constituencies may increase perceived importance without making the submitted reasoning better. This fingerprint is prominent in R44's 120-member working group and R56's representation of 29 elected sheriffs.
species.upstream_parent: Organizational mobilization capacity and representational standing

species.name: Emotional advocacy intensity
species.instruction: Score 10 for repeated alarm, outrage, moral condemnation, emphatic praise, all-caps, exclamation marks, or vivid metaphors; score 0 for consistently restrained, neutral prose.
species.rationale: Emotion can make a comment salient while supplying no additional support for its claims. R22 uses highly charged language about pets and death, and R42 describes a 'crafty bureaucrat's tool' and catastrophic ruin.
species.upstream_parent: Advocacy-campaign messaging norms

species.name: Testimonial narrative framing
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment unfolds as a story about a person, place, community, or unfolding harm before reaching its request; score 0 when it begins with a compact docket-specific issue list or technical disposition table.
species.rationale: Narrative structure can create memorability and apparent human importance without improving policy analysis. R19 begins with school and diving experiences, while R36 frames the issue through a fourth-generation farmer's personal situation.
species.upstream_parent: Grassroots or community mobilization using testimonial storytelling

species.name: Multi-issue agenda bundling
species.instruction: Score 10 when one comment combines several related policy campaigns, controversies, or reform demands into a broad agenda; score 0 when it addresses one narrowly defined provision or implementation question.
species.rationale: Breadth can look substantive to a dense reader while partly reflecting an organization's preexisting agenda rather than relevance to the docket. R07 bundles nitrate, genetic-engineering, and poultry-production demands; R10 combines numerous sanctuary, climate, wildlife, and economic themes.
species.upstream_parent: Lobbying organizations pursuing a standing agenda across multiple rulemakings

species.name: Litigation posture
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment frames the issue through court cases, incorporation by reference, administrative-record preservation, constitutional or APA objections, or accusations of unlawful agency action; score 0 when it contains no adversarial legal posture.
species.rationale: A litigation-oriented voice may appear consequential because it highlights legal vulnerability, not because its policy reasoning is sound. R36 invokes a court case and alleged unlawful board conduct, while R55 argues appointments-clause and APA issues.
species.upstream_parent: Legal counsel involvement and defensive preparation for regulatory litigation

species.name: Tailored-relief seeking
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment seeks a submitter-specific exemption, extension, participation opportunity, applicability carve-out, phased schedule, or cost adjustment; score 0 when it requests only general policy treatment.
species.rationale: A concrete self-interested ask can produce a strong salience signal even when the requested exception is not substantively justified. R06 requests a 60-month exemption extension, R24 seeks a utilization-based compliance schedule, and R30 requests inclusion in future pricing models.
species.upstream_parent: Submitter's material exposure and lobbying for individualized regulatory relief
